Chart patterns

Patterns read from the peaks, troughs and lines that many candles form, pointing to a possible reversal or continuation of the trend.

  • Head and Shoulders

    • Chart pattern
    • ↓ Bearish reversal
    • Multi-candle

    A reversal pattern that forms at the end of an uptrend and is made of three peaks.

  • Inverse Head and Shoulders

    • Chart pattern
    • ↑ Bullish reversal
    • Multi-candle

    A reversal pattern that forms at the end of a downtrend and is made of three troughs.

  • Double Top

    • Chart pattern
    • ↓ Bearish reversal
    • Multi-candle

    A reversal pattern that forms at the end of an uptrend, when price makes two peaks at roughly the same level.

  • Double Bottom

    • Chart pattern
    • ↑ Bullish reversal
    • Multi-candle

    A reversal pattern that forms at the end of a downtrend, when price makes two troughs at roughly the same level.

  • Triple Top

    • Chart pattern
    • ↓ Bearish reversal
    • Multi-candle

    A reversal pattern that forms at the end of an uptrend, when price makes three peaks at roughly the same level.

  • Triple Bottom

    • Chart pattern
    • ↑ Bullish reversal
    • Multi-candle

    A reversal pattern that forms at the end of a downtrend, when price makes three troughs at roughly the same level.

  • Ascending Triangle

    • Chart pattern
    • ↑ Bullish continuation
    • Multi-candle

    A triangle pattern formed by a flat resistance line and a series of rising lows.

  • Descending Triangle

    • Chart pattern
    • ↓ Bearish continuation
    • Multi-candle

    A triangle pattern formed by a flat support line and a series of falling highs.

  • Symmetrical Triangle

    • Chart pattern
    • Continuation with the trend
    • Multi-candle

    A triangle pattern formed by lower highs and higher lows converging on each other.

  • Rectangle

    • Chart pattern
    • Continuation with the trend
    • Multi-candle

    A pattern formed when price moves back and forth between two flat levels for a while.

  • Rising Wedge

    • Chart pattern
    • ↓ Bearish reversal
    • Multi-candle

    A pattern in which both lines slope upwards and converge to the right.

  • Falling Wedge

    • Chart pattern
    • ↑ Bullish reversal
    • Multi-candle

    A pattern in which both lines slope downwards and converge to the right.

  • Flag

    • Chart pattern
    • Continuation with the trend
    • Multi-candle

    A continuation pattern that forms when a sharp, fast move (the pole) is followed by a short pause in a narrow channel sloping against that move.

  • Pennant

    • Chart pattern
    • Continuation with the trend
    • Multi-candle

    A short pause that forms after a sharp, fast move (the pole) and is made of two small, converging lines.
